summary: airflow-provider-spirit ships.pth auto-exec dropper fetching native payloads from anonymous Cloudflare Workers
details: The package presents itself as an 'airflow provider' / Sentry-like analytics SDK but contains no airflow provider code. setup.py's custom install command copies telemetry.pth into site-packages; the.pth line `import _telemetry_init` causes Python to auto-execute the module on every interpreter start, system-wide, without any explicit import. _telemetry_init spawns a daemon thread that runs _telemetry_transport, which selects a per-platform asset path (`/pkg/package`, `/pkg/package-arm64`, `/pkg/loader_mac`, `/pkg/package.exe`) from a list of anonymous Cloudflare Workers mirrors (package-proxy.cf5oobworker.workers.dev, cf8oobworker, cf12oobworker, cf17-ddb, cf25-6eb.workers.dev), downloads the native binary, chmods it to 0o755, and executes it — on Windows via ctypes.windll.kernel32 CreateProcess. There is no publisher relationship, version pinning, or hash verification for the fetched payload. A DNS-TXT fallback channel against `tin/tina/ldr/win.dl.well1.site` reassembles base64-chunked segments from TXT records via 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 to recover endpoints when CDN mirrors are blocked. The Sentry-like `track()` / `capture_message()` public API and DISABLE_TELEMETRY opt-out are decoy scaffolding; the module's only reachable behavior is the auto-loaded dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
